subject: Azure private listing — procurement questions and negotiated terms
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@blueridge-fin.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Peter Farrell <peter.farrell@blueridge-fin.com>; Anita Suresh <anita.suresh@microsoft.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure private listing — procurement questions and negotiated terms

Thanks for the quick follow-up, Dylan. We reviewed the private offer packet your team submitted and have a few procurement and legal items we need clarified before we proceed with an internal approval. High level: pricing footprint, invoicing, audit evidence, and some contract redlines.

Specific asks: 
- Can Redwood issue invoices directly to BlueRidge (non-Marketplace invoicing) under a purchase order? If not, we need confirmation the Marketplace private offer flow supports invoice to customer / PO references (our systems require PO on invoice).
- Data residency: we need assurance that any PII or transaction metadata for our customers is retained only in us-east and will not be replicated to non-US regions. Please point to docs or a SOC2 artifact if available.
- Indemnity and limitation: our counsel flagged section 7 (third-party claims) in the draft terms; Peter will propose language but wanted to know if Redwood can accept a carve-out for regulated financial services with a cap tied to fees rather than a flat multiple.
- SLA credits: BlueRidge requires a financial credit mechanism for sustained latency regressions (not just single outages). Current SLA in your draft is uptime-only.
- Co-sell registration: Anita, do you have visibility on whether co-sell listing on Azure Marketplace will require additional paperwork from BlueRidge? We prefer the private offer to be co-sell enabled but want to understand any MS requirements for joint GTM.

I attached our procurement checklist and a short RFI. Can we get a follow-up call early next week to walk through these? Thanks — Sarah

Attachments: BR-Procurement-RFI.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@blueridge-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Anita Suresh <anita.suresh@microsoft.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure private listing — procurement questions and negotiated terms

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate Peter looping legal. Quick answers up front, then I suggest a 30-minute sync Tues morning PST to go line-by-line.

1) Invoicing/PO: Redwood can support invoice-to-customer for Dedicated and Private customers. For Azure private offers the recommended path is to use the Marketplace billing flow (simpler for co-sell), but we can support direct invoicing if BlueRidge requires it. I’ll confirm the operational steps (AP contact, PO reference field, tax IDs) with finance and get back by EOD.

2) Data residency: Redwood Private deployments can be pinned to a VNet in us-east; all customer data and logs for that deployment are resident in-region. For the hosted private listing variant we rely on Azure region placement; we will add language to the data processing Addendum confirming no cross-region backups for BlueRidge. SOC2 Type II is available — I’ll share the evidence.

3) Indemnity/limitation: We’re open to a fee-tied cap for regulated customers. Markus (legal) — can you draft proposed text that limits liability to fees paid in prior 12 months, with carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct?

4) SLA credits: We can add a latency-based degradation credit and define sustained regression as >3 consecutive days of P95 latency > X ms for production routes. Marissa, can you propose a metric and credit % that maps to typical production workloads?

5) Co-sell: Anita — if co-sell is feasible we’ll need to register the Azure private offer; BlueRidge indicated they want joint GTM. Anita, could you advise required paperwork and expected timelines?

Proposed times for a sync: Tues 17 Feb 09:00 PST or 11:00 PST. I’ll attach a marked-up private offer doc with our suggested edits.

Best,
Dylan

Attachment: Redwood-Azure-PrivatePlan-Terms-20260214.docx

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@blueridge-fin.com>, Peter Farrell <peter.farrell@blueridge-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure private listing — procurement questions and negotiated terms

Sarah / Peter — looping in on legal points. Per Dylan, Redwood is prepared to offer a liability cap tied to fees with the usual carve-outs. Draft language below (quick, for discussion):

"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Redwood's aggregate liability for claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months preceding the date the claim arose, except in cases of gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of confidentiality or data protection obligations."

We can accept a customer-friendly cap for regulated financial services provided BlueRidge agrees to forego certain enhanced indemnities (we'd like to avoid unconstrained exposure). On the indemnity for third-party IP claims, Redwood requests the customer provides prompt notice and sole control of defense with reasonable cooperation.

I will prepare a redline of the draft terms and circulate by end of day. If BlueRidge has specific language from their master services agreement, please share so we can reconcile.

Thanks,
Markus

(On a process note: if BlueRidge requires direct vendor invoicing, finance will need to confirm tax/PO fields — that may add a week to the procurement timeline.)

From: Peter Farrell <peter.farrell@blueridge-fin.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>; Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>; Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@blueridge-fin.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Azure private listing — procurement questions and negotiated terms

Markus — thanks for the proposed cap. A couple of quick notes from BlueRidge legal: 
- We prefer the cap be expressed as "the greater of $X or fees paid in the prior 12 months" for operational predictability. Can Redwood provide a baseline $X?
- For indemnity defense control: BlueRidge cannot cede sole defense in cases where parallel claims may affect our financial services licenses. We would accept joint-control with predefined escalation rights.

We will compile our preferred redlines and circulate by EOD Wednesday. On invoicing, we prefer PO-based invoices from the vendor (Redwood) rather than Marketplace billing — that aligns with our procurement policies. If Redwood can accept that, we can expedite approval.

Regards,
Peter

--
Peter Farrell
Legal Counsel, BlueRidge Financial

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@blueridge-fin.com>, Peter Farrell <peter.farrell@blueridge-fin.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Anita Suresh <anita.suresh@microsoft.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure private listing — procurement questions and negotiated terms

Sarah / Peter — quick update after internal review and a short sync with Anita this morning. Action items and concessions we can commit to today: 

1) Invoicing: Redwood Finance confirms we can issue vendor invoices with PO reference for BlueRidge private offer. We will need BlueRidge's W-9 and billing contact. Treasury has indicated this adds ~5 business days to onboarding for routing.

2) Data residency & SOC2: Attached is a redacted SOC2 Type II report (summary) and a statement we will include in the DPA specifying region-limited storage to us-east for the BlueRidge deployment. No cross-region backups without prior consent.

3) Liability cap: Redwood can offer a hybrid cap: the greater of $500,000 or fees paid in prior 12 months. Markus will include the joint-control defense language for IP claims per Peter's note.

4) SLA credits: Proposal — P95 latency credit schedule: if P95 exceeds 600ms for 3 consecutive days, credit = 5% of monthly fees; 10% if >3 regressions in a 30-day window. We can further tune thresholds after a short performance baseline test.

5) Co-sell on Azure: Anita confirmed co-sell is possible with a private offer; Microsoft requires a Marketplace publisher registration and a co-sell registration form (Anita will send). Timeline for co-sell activation is typically 2-3 weeks after registration.

Next steps: Dylan/Markus will send a redline of the private offer doc and a separate DPA with the residency clause. Sarah — if BlueRidge can provide W-9 and billing contact, we will prepare vendor invoice sample and DocuSign-ready agreement. Can we target signature by end of next week?

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if any of this needs faster resolution.

Regards,
Marissa

Attachments referenced: Redwood-Azure-PrivatePlan-Terms-20260214.docx, Redwood-SOC2-summary-redacted.pdf
